narrative.bottom_line: The expansion is intact but narrowing, and the regime model's mid-cycle label with a composite of 0.175 rests on equity momentum and a positive curve rather than on hiring, which has stalled. A commodity-led price surge is the tension. Pricing power, not operating leverage, is being rewarded.
paragraphs: Real GDP of 2.2% masks a labour market that has stopped adding jobs. Nonfarm payrolls added 29,000 in September, down 104,000 from the prior month, leaving hiring at stall speed. Initial claims of 194,000 sit at the bottom of their 20-year range, so employers are hoarding workers, not firing. Consumer sentiment at 48.1 sits near a 74-year low even as retail sales grow 6.29% annually.

Inflation is re-accelerating through commodities while long Treasury yields sit near two-decade highs. Core PCE at 3.01% has edged up while headline CPI of 3.72% climbs, the gap all energy and food. Brent crude at $115 a barrel and copper at a 35-year record are re-inflating input costs. The 10-year Treasury at 4.96% ranks in the 99th percentile of 20 years, repricing every long-dated asset.

Credit is open at the top of the stack and closing fast at the bottom. High-yield OAS widened 72bp in a month to 3.40%, the 86th percentile of three years. CCC spreads jumped to 13.4% from 10.93% while AAA barely moved, a clean split by quality. The Chicago Fed financial conditions index at -0.496 still reads accommodative, so distress is borrower-specific, not systemic.
watch: Unemployment above 4.6% would trigger the Sahm rule and end the no-layoffs expansion.
Five-year, five-year forward inflation above 2.5% would show the commodity surge leaking into expectations.
High-yield spreads past 450bp would push distress beyond CCC borrowers into mainstream corporate funding.

sectors.influence: The 10-year Treasury at 4.96% lifts the discount rate on distant earnings, where tech's value sits. The AI capex cycle offsets that by filling order books. At 8.9% above its 200-day average, the ETF prices capex over duration.
sectors.headline: Capex outruns the discount rate

sectors.influence: The 10-year to 2-year spread at 31bp is positive but sits in the 27th percentile of two decades, a thin lending margin. Investment-grade spreads at 89bp hint at provisioning ahead. Curve normalisation and credit risk roughly cancel.
sectors.headline: Banks squeeze a thin curve

sectors.influence: Job openings falling to 7.08 million cools the growth trade and sends capital toward predictable earnings. Healthcare's defensive cash flows plus aging-demographics volume growth compound that. Relative strength of 8.3% over three months confirms the rotation is underway.
sectors.headline: Defence wins by default

sectors.influence: Retail gasoline at $4.28 a gallon drains disposable income just as the savings rate sits at 4.1%, the 8th percentile of 68 years. Rate-geared big-ticket demand, the sector's best structural lever, stays locked. The ETF trades below its 200-day average.
sectors.headline: Pumped dry at the pump

sectors.influence: Global food prices in the 96th percentile of 35 years squeeze packaged-goods margins, but proven pricing power passes costs through. Stalled hiring is pushing capital into predictable cash flows. One-month relative strength of 9.7% shows the defensive bid winning.
sectors.headline: Pricing power earns its keep

sectors.influence: Consumer sentiment near its 74-year low threatens advertising budgets, this sector's revenue engine. Elevated long rates compress growth multiples further, and the retail-media mix shift cannot offset both. Six-month relative strength of -16.3% confirms the derating.
sectors.headline: Ad budgets meet dear money

sectors.influence: Industrial production growing 2.25% a year is too slow to absorb iron and steel producer prices up 66%, so margins compress. Reshoring and defence capex offer a multi-year floor. A 12.7% three-month relative-strength shortfall says the cost squeeze dominates.
sectors.headline: Steel costs grind the gears

sectors.influence: WTI crude at $107.89, the 96th percentile of 20 years, flows straight to cash flow under post-2015 capital discipline. A broad dollar index at the 90th percentile caps the upside. A 20% premium to the 200-day average says price wins.
sectors.headline: Crude does the heavy lifting

sectors.influence: Copper at a 35-year record price lifts miner revenue, and electrification demand keeps the deficit structural. Housing starts of 1.22 million, the 25th percentile of 68 years, cut construction volumes. Flat relative strength says the two forces offset.
sectors.headline: Copper up, cranes down

sectors.influence: The 30-year Treasury at 5.29% offers competing income and raises the cost of funding rate-base capex. Data-centre load growth lifts allowed spending for the first time in a generation. Three-month underperformance of 10.4% says yield competition still rules.
sectors.headline: Bonds outbid the dividend

sectors.influence: Mortgage rates at 7.32% and BBB spreads at 111bp raise refinancing costs faster than leases reprice. Data-centre and logistics demand supports rents at the better end. A three-month shortfall of 10.3% says financing costs dominate.
sectors.headline: Cap rates meet a wall
